source.title: Network dynamics-based framework for understanding deep neural networks
source.authors: Yuchen Lin; Si-Han Feng; Yong Zhang; Hong Zhao

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including its appendix; no relevant section appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports grokking results and argues that its mechanisms differ between deep and shallow networks, refining the usual memorization-to-generalization account.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking-like delayed test-accuracy improvements on MNIST, plus conditions in which grokking is absent. It does not test small algorithmic datasets or whether delay grows as the training set shrinks. Other reported accuracy, RPD, basin, architecture, and hyperparameter results are omitted unless they directly describe the grokking behavior or its tested conditions.
record.test_reason: The study reports grokking-like delayed test-accuracy jumps on MNIST, a non-algorithmic dataset, in deep ReLU nets with batch norm and in a reproduced large-init shallow setup. It shows the deep-net delay disappears when batch-norm evaluation statistics are replaced by batch statistics. It argues deep-net grokking is a batch-norm/phase-transition effect rather than memorization-to-generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the record blurs a contrast. The authors say a learning-phase transition is a prerequisite for grokking. In DNNs, grokking arises from the BN evaluation mode: running statistics mismatch test data after the phase transition, which differs from memorization-to-generalization. In shallow networks it comes from an abrupt expansion of attraction basins, which they say aligns with the conventional memorization-to-generalization view. They also argue avoiding grokking (starting in phase II) gives optimal performance more efficiently.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes MNIST networks using RPDs, attraction basins, batch normalization, and training trajectories rather than reproducing modular-arithmetic grokking experiments. It reports a shallow-network setup attributed to cited work and separate DNN experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking varies with the tested optimizer, learning rate, batch size, activation, batch-normalization mode, and whether a phase transition occurs. The text does not establish systematic initialization-scale or weight-norm effects.

fits_no_version.finding: In the 23-layer DNN, test projections lie outside training regions before grokking and overlap after. With BN training-mode statistics they overlap throughout and no delay occurs. The authors attribute deep-net grokking to stale BN running statistics after a learning-phase transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking-like delays in batch-normalized deep networks can be an evaluation artifact of BN running statistics lagging behind a training phase transition, and disappear when batch statistics are used at test time.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking runs do not reach higher final accuracy: R1 grokking reaches 97.14%, while R4 without grokking reaches 97.89%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is not required for, and may be a slower route to, the best generalization.

record.peer_reviewed: Science China Physics Mechanics and Astronomy
record.problems: The paper gives no exact grokking delay or test-accuracy values in the text for these configurations; key trajectories are presented in figures. The shallow-network example uses 1000 samples but does not sweep dataset size. Initialization scale and weight decay are not systematically varied in the reported grokking comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported accuracy, RPD, and attraction-basin results were left out because they do not directly measure delayed test generalization or a condition that changes its occurrence.

untested.parts: Initialization scale or weight norm is never varied to switch grokking on or off. No lazy-to-rich transition is studied. No non-image data such as text or molecules is used.
No algorithmic datasets and no training-set-size sweep of the delay.
No circuit identification. RPD gradients are tracked, but not as a test of whether progress measures anticipate a generalizing circuit.
No critical dataset size and no ungrokking. The weight-norm shrink before grokking (Fig. 7g) is observed but weight decay is not varied.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and softmax floating-point limits are not examined.

missing.what: In the shallow large-init net, weight norm shrinks rapidly just before grokking. Sample- and weight-space basin sizes jump from ~10^-2 to above 10^-1 at grokking onset. Test accuracy later declines with continued training.
23-layer DNN final/peak test accuracy is not stated in text; the delay length for any run is figure-only.

record.verdict_notes: The shallow setup reproduces Liu et al. (Omnigrok, arXiv:2210.01117), which is not listed as an original source, so a verdict is allowed. The BN artifact resembles V7's artifact theme but is neither an optimizer instability nor floating-point precision, so it is kept outside V7. No uncertainties or seeds are reported; all evidence is figure-based with text descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset, modular arithmetic task, or training-set-size sweep testing whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

No identifiable generalizing circuit such as a Fourier algorithm is traced, and the study does not test whether memorizing components are removed later or whether a continuous measure anticipates the test-accuracy jump.

The paper reports grokking-like delays on MNIST and compares some conditions with and without grokking. It does not systematically compare initialization scales or weight norms to establish that those choices switch grokking on or off, nor does it study a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic large-model data is studied.
Weight decay is used in one shallow-network setup, but the study does not test an efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs or test convergence to the same algorithm.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax, or whether controlling them removes grokking.

rows.subject: 23-layer DNN (width 128)
rows.operation_detail: Compare two-dimensional projections of training and test samples before and after grokking using bottleneck directions obtained from the original final-layer weights.
rows.measure: Overlap of test-sample and training-sample projection regions.
rows.baseline: Before grokking, test samples are projected outside the region occupied by training samples.
rows.value: After grokking, the test and training projection regions overlap substantially.
rows.note: The authors connect the overlap to the abrupt rise in test accuracy.
rows.check: This row is a mechanistic visualization: 2D bottleneck projection overlap of test vs training samples. It is not a measure of delayed generalization itself, so it does not bear on a version as named. It is recorded under fits_no_version.

conditions.value: before and after the corresponding grokking period

rows.measure: Whether delayed test-accuracy improvement and the associated test-to-training projection shift occur.
rows.baseline: Evaluation mode shows grokking and a post-grokking shift into the training-sample projection regions.

rows.locator: Section V.A; Fig. 6(e)–(f) and accompanying text
rows.note: The paper states that applying training mode at test time eliminates the conditions necessary for grokking in this case.

relationships.condition: Deep BN networks on MNIST: other learning rates, batch sizes or linear activation, and test-time BN training-mode statistics
relationships.reason: In deep nets the delay depends on learning rate, batch size and activation (absent in R4–R7). It also vanishes when BN batch statistics are used at test (R9). So it hinges on BN evaluation statistics and a learning-phase transition, not on init scale or weight norm.
relationships.display_finding: Delays disappeared under alternative learning rates, batch sizes or linear activation, and when batch normalization used batch statistics during testing.
